primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type II due to SLC35C1 deficiency
mechanism: SLC35C1 encodes the Golgi GDP-fucose transporter. Deficiency prevents normal fucosylation of leukocyte glycans, including sialyl-Lewis X selectin ligands, impairing selectin-mediated leukocyte rolling and extravasation.
vignette: A 3-year-old boy has recurrent bacterial infections, persistent neutrophilia when well, poor growth, and developmental delay. Wounds contain little pus. Flow-based testing shows markedly impaired neutrophil rolling on activated endothelium, but beta-2 integrin expression is normal. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC35C1.
lead: Which of the following molecular abnormalities most directly explains this child's impaired leukocyte recruitment?
correct: Defective Golgi transport of GDP-fucose causing deficient fucosylation of selectin ligands such as sialyl-Lewis X
distractors: Deficiency of the beta-2 integrin CD18 causing failure of firm leukocyte adhesion
Deficiency of myeloperoxidase causing impaired generation of hypochlorous acid
Defective NADPH oxidase assembly causing failure of the respiratory burst
Deficiency of C3 causing impaired complement-mediated opsonization
distractor_notes: CD18 deficiency causes LAD type I and failure of firm adhesion rather than the selectin-ligand rolling defect described here.
Myeloperoxidase deficiency affects intracellular microbial killing after phagocytosis, not endothelial rolling.
Chronic granulomatous disease affects oxidative killing and does not cause a primary selectin-mediated rolling defect.
C3 deficiency impairs complement functions but does not explain normal beta-2 integrins with abnormal neutrophil rolling and SLC35C1 variants.
key_expl: LAD type II is a congenital glycosylation disorder caused by SLC35C1 deficiency. Loss of the Golgi GDP-fucose transporter reduces fucosylation of surface glycans, including sialyl-Lewis X, an important selectin ligand. Leukocytes therefore cannot roll normally along activated endothelium, reducing tissue recruitment and producing recurrent infections with persistent leukocytosis.
objective: Explain LAD type II as defective GDP-fucose transport and selectin-ligand fucosylation causing impaired leukocyte rolling.
